caption: An empty living room lit by a single lamp during a storm brightens for an instant as lightning flashes through the window.

sa.check: An empty living room lit by a single lamp.
A window is in view or its light falls into the room.
The room brightens for an instant, as from a flash outside the window.
A storm shows outside the window: dark sky, rain or streaked glass.
The lamp is lit before, during and after the flash.
The order is lamp-lit, flash, lamp-lit again.

pc.expect: The brightening is brief: the room lights up and returns to its lamp-lit state; flashes may repeat but each ends.
pc.fail: The room stays bright to the end of the clip after the flash; or brightens steadily without ending; or the flash fades in slowly like a dimmer being turned up; or the room ends darker than its lamp-lit state with the lamp still lit.

pc.expect: The flash light enters from the window side: surfaces facing the window brighten most and the far side of the room least.
pc.fail: The whole room brightens evenly with no side brighter; or the brightening comes from the lamp's side while the window side stays as it was; or the window glass stays dark while the room lights up.

pc.expect: Sharp shadows of the window frame appear on the floor or the wall opposite only during the flash and vanish with it; the lamp's own soft shadows remain as before.
pc.fail: The frame's shadow stays on the wall after the room has returned to lamp light; or the shadow appears before the flash; or the shadow lies on the window side of the objects rather than away from the window.

pc.expect: Nothing in the room moves at the flash: furniture, pictures, the lamp and the curtains stay as they were, apart from curtains stirring in a draught.
pc.fail: Furniture or pictures shift at the flash; or the lamp moves or swings; or a door opens by itself; or the curtains fly up sharply at the instant of the flash while nothing else stirs.

pc.expect: The room's contents are the same before, during and after the flash: the flash reveals what was there and creates or removes nothing.
pc.fail: Furniture or pictures appear or vanish between the dim and lit frames; or the lamp vanishes or duplicates; or the window moves along the wall; or the room's layout changes after the flash.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: Wall colours, the lampshade and the curtains keep their colours apart from brightness.
pc.fail: The walls change colour rather than brightness; or the lampshade changes colour; or the curtains change pattern.
